name: tpl-chain-response-1-goal
task: Carry the box to the exit. Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task commands to pick up the box again on the very next move after it falls, but the Response clause only says holding_box on that step or later, not on the next move.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires holding_box to happen at least once, but the only Existence is the hard Existence(holding_box) for the task's wording, not for the task's requirement. Add a hard Precedence to make the earlier steps happen: the last hard step of the chain is the last hard Existence(holding_box). Keep the hard Existence(holding_box) and the hard Response(box_fell, holding_box).

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the box to be picked up again on the very next move after the box falls. The Response clause requires the box to be picked up after it falls, but it can be on the same step or later. The task requires the agent to pick it up again immediately. Add a ChainResponse clause to make the agent pick up the box on the very next move after it falls.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the agent to carry the box to the exit, but the first clause does not force the agent to pick it up; the first clause alone does not capture the task of carrying the box. Add a hard Existence(box_fell) next to the hard Existence(holding_box) to make the agent pick it up and then keep it; keep the hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) as the rule for picking it up again on the very next move.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the agent to pick up the box again on the very next move after it falls. The current ChainResponse does not enforce this, because it does not require the agent to pick up the box again on the very next step. Instead, it only requires that the agent holds the box on the very next step after the box falls. To fix this, you need to add a new clause that requires the agent to pick up the box again on the very next move after it falls. This can be done by adding a new ChainResponse that has box_fell as the trigger and holding_box as the goal, but with a priority of 'hard' and a ChainResponse instead of a Response, to require the agent to pick up the box again on the very next move after it falls.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the agent to carry the box to the exit, but the machine has no way to make holding_box happen after the agent picks up the box, because the first pickup of the episode starts the first fall, and later pickups cause no fall. Add a hard Precedence(holding_box, box_fell) to make box_fell always happen after holding_box. The machine already rewards the agent for reaching the exit with the box in its hands, but it never rewards the agent for carrying the box to the exit. Add a hard Existence(holding_box) to make the machine reward the agent for carrying the box to the exit. The machine will now reward the agent for reaching the exit with the box in its hands, and also for carrying the box to the exit.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task asks the agent to carry the box to the exit, but the hard Existence clause only requires that the agent holds the box at least once, not that it reaches the exit with the box. The task also asks the agent to pick up the box again after it falls, but the hard ChainResponse clause only requires that the agent picks up the box on the very next step after it falls, not that it picks it up after every fall. The task requires that the box is in the agent's hands when it reaches the exit, which is not guaranteed by the given clauses.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task commands the agent to carry the box to the exit, and the box falls. The hard Existence(holding_box) clause is correct, but it does not account for the box falling and the agent picking it up again. The task requires the agent to pick up the box on its very next move when it falls, but the hard Existence(holding_box) clause does not capture this requirement. The compiler's clue 'Every way to finish includes: holding_box' is not sufficient to ensure that the agent picks up the box on its next move. To fix this, the agent needs a soft ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) clause to capture the requirement that the agent picks up the box on its very next move when it falls. The existing hard Existence(holding_box) clause should be kept, as it ensures that the agent carries the box to the exit. The corrected set of clauses should be: hard Existence(holding_box), soft ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box).

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the box to be carried to the exit, but the clause only requires holding_box, which is only one step before the exit. The task also requires the box to be picked up again on the very next move after it falls. The clause does not require the agent to move to pick up the box again. Add a ChainResponse between pickup and box_fell to require the agent to pick up the box again immediately after it falls.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: the task requires carrying the box to the exit with ChainResponse for the box falls, which the machine implements with a reward of 11 for the exit step, and a reward of -10 for any step that breaks the hard ChainResponse.
